scope.flow: launchFor() initial liquidity calculation in Bonding.sol
scope.environment: Solidity smart contract (Bonding.sol) using integer division

statements.text: K is a contract constant equal to 3×10^12.
assetRate is a value set during initialization.
supply is the total supply of the new token.
launchFor() computes the assetToken liquidity amount via the bonding curve formula using integer division.
The computed liquidity is used to pair with the newly minted token supply for initial liquidity provision.

Integer division truncates remainders at the first division (K * 10000) / assetRate and within the second line (((k * 10000 ether) / supply) * 1 ether) / 10000, losing fractional parts when the numerator is not perfectly divisible by the denominator.
The calculated liquidity amount deviates from the mathematically precise value intended by the bonding curve formula.

The bonding curve's mathematical relationship between token supply, price, and reserves is broken, potentially affecting fairness and predictability for early participants and liquidity providers.
Subsequent trades on a pool initialized with an incorrect liquidity ratio may experience unexpected slippage versus the theoretical bonding curve price.
launchFor() should compute the liquidity amount equal to the mathematically precise bonding curve value, without truncation-induced deviation.
The supply-to-liquidity ratio used for the initial DEX pair should match the bonding curve's intended initial price.
